speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Could you describe the specific feeding difficulties your 8-month-old son is experiencing, and when did they first begin? Also, has he been vomiting, and if so, is the vomit green or yellow?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has your baby passed any stool or gas in the last 24 hours, and is the stool normal or bloody? Additionally, does he have a fever?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has your baby passed any stool or gas in the last 24 hours, and if so, has the stool appeared bloody or like "red currant jelly"? I also need to know if you feel any distinct abdominal mass when examining his belly.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the lack of stool, worsening abdominal distension, and feeding refusal, I need to check for an intussusception or obstruction. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound. I also want to see if there is a palpable sausage-shaped mass. REQUEST IMAGES.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal Ultrasound and palpation for a sausage-shaped mass were not performed as they are not included in the available data. However, existing test results show: Abdominal X-ray reveals dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction. Barium Enema findings show a transition zone in the distal colon, compatible with Hirschsprung disease. Vital signs indicate a heart rate of 120 bpm and respiratory rate of 30 breaths/min, both noted as normal for age, with abdominal examination confirming distension and tenderness in the left lower quadrant.

speaker: Doctor
text: The barium enema findings of a transition zone in the distal colon strongly point to Hirschsprung disease, and the abdominal X-ray confirms an obstruction. Given this clear diagnostic evidence, I have enough information to proceed. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung disease.
